newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH FEB CPI EASES, C.BANK WARNS NO RATE CUT NEAR.
newsitem.headline: CZECH FEB CPI EASES, C.BANK WARNS NO RATE CUT NEAR.

text.p: Czech consumer inflation eased to an all-time low in February, but the central bank said it was still too early to consider any loosening of its tight monetary policy.

The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) said on Monday that month-on-month CPI eased to 0.3 percent from 1.2 percent in January, a typically high inflation month, putting the year-on- year figure at 7.3 percent, the lowest since the Czech Republic became independent, down from 7.4 percent the previous month.
The key sliding average inflation figure, which uses 1993 as a base, edged down to 8.6 percent from 8.7 percent in January, and was down from 9.1 percent in February 1996.

"No, no, no. Only after the central bank will be sure that inflation pressures are, I would say weaker, could it consider some changes in monetary policy, but this is not the case now," CNB spokesman Martin Svehla told Reuters.

Last summer the CNB raised its key discount rate one percentage point to 10.5 percent, and hiked minimum reserve requirements to 11.5 percent from 8.5 percent of deposits to squeeze off surging domestic demand.
Analysts said the moves, which were coupled along with a rise in minimum reserve requirements, served to significantly restrict growth of the money supply and ease inflationary pressures.

"The figure is encouraging, though we expect that inflation will slow throughout the first half of the year because of the central bank's monetary tightening moves last year," said Boris Gomez, a macro-economic analyst at ING Barings.
Added Miroslav Soucek, an analyst at bank IPB: "The figures appear to prove the positive results of the CNB's monetary policy...They are very favourable."
Growth in the money supply stood at +9.7 percent in November, well below the central bank's 13 to 17 percent growth target for 1996, and in the middle of its 8-12 percent range for 1997.
But central bank officials have warned that wage growth -- which was up 14.4 percent in nominal terms in January -- and its influence on inflation is a growing concern.
"Question marks may come to the forefront in the second half when we will have a better idea of wage growth and some price deregulations," Gomez added.
CSU figures show price deregulation influenced the seasonally-adjusted rate by 0.63 percent, while seasonally-adjusted core inflation was 0.34 percent.
Analysts said that they were pleasantly surprised with CSU figures showing that prices foodstuffs, drinks and tobacco, which usually pushes inflation up, was unchanged, month-on-month.
The Czech crown also reacted favourably to the inflation figures, and was boosted further by Svehla's subsequent interest rate comments.
In afternoon trading, the crown was at 29.149 against the dollar and 17.085 to the mark, implying +2.42 percent against the basket midpoint, down from an opening at +2.05 percent.
At midday, the central bank followed the early uptrend with its daily fixing, putting the crown/dollar at 29.190 and crown/mark at 17.087, or +2.36 against the basket.
